{{Wireless adapter |brand=D-Link |model=DWL-120+ |revision=A1 |upc=790069245404 |ean= |asin=B00006HY17 |price= |est_release_date= |fcc_date=04/23/2003 |manuf_country=Taiwan |is_manuf=No |manuf=Global Sun |manuf_model=GL2422MU-MT |manuf_rev= |availability= |if=USB |if_bus_version=1.1 |if_connector_type=Female Mini-B |form_factor=corded (modular) adapter |vendor_id=2001 |device_id=3b01 |subvendor_id= |subdevice_id= |id_string= |fcc_id=O7J-GL2422MU-MT |ic_id= |chip1_brand=Texas Instruments |chip1_model=TNETW1100B |chip2_brand=Maxim |chip2_model=MAX2820 |chip3_brand= |chip3_model= |chip4_brand= |chip4_model= |addl_chips=2.4GHz Power Amplifier IC;GATAX;GA2P4W22;G, W22, B004E, P01;1; |accessible_UART=No |flags= |ant_conn= |802dot11_protocols=b |txchains= |rxchains= |sstreams= |oui=00:0D:88, 00:40:05 |lin_driver= |win_driver= }} The FCC docs show the device with either a '''GATAX''' or '''RFMD''' power amplifier. The one in use seems to be the '''GATAX''' module.
There would appear to be an additional version with an FCC ID of [[FCC ID::KA2DWL-120PLUS]]. Both are Global Sun GL2422MUs.
